title: Handle, transport, store and utilize hazardous materials on a civil construction site

lessons.title: Knowing hazardous materials
lessons.html:
Knowing hazardous materials

Construction work happens on farms and grain sites too: new silo bases, roads, dam walls, canals, sheds. On these sites workers handle hazardous materials. These are materials that can hurt people, start fires or harm the environment.

Common hazardous materials on site

  • Diesel and petrol: catch fire easily, fumes are harmful.
  • Cement and wet concrete: burn the skin and eyes, dust harms the lungs.
  • Bitumen and tar: applied hot, cause burns.
  • Paints, thinners and solvents: flammable, fumes cause dizziness.
  • Gas cylinders (acetylene, LPG, oxygen): fire and explosion risk.
  • Explosives for blasting rock: only licensed blasters may handle them.
  • Curing compounds, form oil, acids for cleaning.

Reading labels and signs

Every container of a hazardous material must have a label. The label tells you:

  • The name of the product.
  • Hazard pictures (pictograms): for example a flame for flammable, a skull for toxic, a corroded hand for corrosive.
  • Warnings and safety instructions.
  • What PPE to wear and what to do in an accident.

More details are in the safety data sheet (SDS). Your supervisor keeps the SDS for each product on site. Ask to see it.

Rules

  • Never use a material if the label is missing or you cannot read it. Tell your supervisor.
  • Never put a hazardous material into a cooldrink bottle or food container. Someone could drink it.
  • Keep materials in their own marked containers.
  • Do not mix two chemicals together unless the label or your supervisor says so. Some mixtures give off poison gas or catch fire.

If you do not understand a label, ask. It is always better to ask than to guess.

lessons.title: Transporting, storing and using hazardous materials safely
lessons.html:
Transporting, storing and using safely

Transporting on site

  • Close lids tightly before moving containers.
  • Tie containers down on the bakkie or trailer so they cannot fall or roll.
  • Gas cylinders travel upright and secured, with valve caps on.
  • Do not carry fuel inside the cab with people.
  • Keep a fire extinguisher on vehicles that carry fuel.
  • No smoking near the vehicle.

Storing

  • Store fuel and flammables in a ventilated, marked store, away from offices, heat and sparks. Put up No Smoking signs.
  • Put fuel tanks and drums in a bund (a wall or tray) that can hold a spill.
  • Keep cement bags dry, on pallets.
  • Store gas cylinders upright, chained, in the shade. Keep oxygen apart from fuel gas.
  • Lock the store. Keep a list of what is in it.

Using

  1. Read the label and know the hazards.
  2. Wear the PPE: gloves, safety glasses, dust mask, overalls, boots. For cement, wear gloves and boots so wet concrete does not stay on your skin.
  3. Use only the amount you need.
  4. Work in fresh air when using solvents or paint.
  5. Close containers after use and return them to the store.
  6. Wash your hands before you eat, drink or smoke.

Spills

  • Warn others and keep them away.
  • Stop the leak if it is safe.
  • Use the spill kit, sand or absorbent to soak it up.
  • Keep spills out of drains, rivers and dams.
  • Report every spill to your supervisor.

First aid basics

If a chemical gets in the eyes, rinse with clean running water for a long time and get medical help. If on the skin, take off the dirty clothes and wash the skin well. Follow the first aid section of the SDS. First aid needs hands-on training by an accredited provider.

Key points

  • Read labels and the SDS before using any hazardous material.
  • Never put chemicals or fuel in food or drink containers.
  • Secure containers and gas cylinders when transporting them.
  • Store flammables in a bunded, ventilated, locked store with no smoking.
  • Wear PPE and clean up and report every spill.
